subject: Post-incident digest: transient session-resync — customer readout & action checklist
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Barker <julia.barker@cedarbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident digest: transient session-resync — customer readout & action checklist

Hi Julia,

Thanks again for the time this morning. I wanted to follow up with a concise, customer-facing summary of the event your team saw on 2026-08-20 (approx. 22:30 UTC): a short window where a subset of inference sessions experienced a "resync" signal that caused token-stream interruptions for ~90 seconds for ~0.8% of requests to your Dedicated pool.

What happened (short):
- Root cause: an internal session state reconciliation job retried unexpectedly during a rolling upgrade, which briefly reattached client sessions to new worker nodes before KV cache hydration completed.
- Customer impact: token streaming paused and some requests received 5xx before automatic retry; most client SDKs recovered without user action.
- Duration: visible between 22:28–22:32 UTC; most traffic recovered by 22:33 UTC.

Attached: a compact timeline (session-resync-timeline.csv) and an RCA summary (rca-summary-cedarbridge.pdf).

Immediate mitigations we executed:
1) Hotfix: disabled the reconciliation retry on the rolling upgrade path (completed 22:40 UTC).
2) Fallback: added a short-lived guard that pins active sessions to prior workers until KV cache warmup completes (deployed 23:05 UTC).
3) Compensating: we disabled aggressive aggressive-prefetch for your Dedicated pool for the next 48 hours to avoid similar warmup contention.

Actions we're committing (owner + ETA):
- Full root-cause report (David) — 2026-08-23 EOD
- Operator playbook update & upgrade gating (Marissa) — 2026-09-03
- SDK resilience guidance (Sofia) — 2026-08-25

Next steps for CedarBridge:
- Please review the attached timeline and flag any client-side errors you still observe.
- If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min technical readout (we have availability Mon/Tue next week).

Apologies for the disruption — we know even short interruptions are costly. We're treating this with high priority and will share the full forensics and remediation plan by 2026-08-23.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Reliability PM | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai

---
Attachment stubs: session-resync-timeline.csv (6 rows), rca-summary-cedarbridge.pdf (4 pages)

From: Julia Barker <julia.barker@cedarbridge.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:49:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident digest: transient session-resync — customer readout & action checklist

Sofia,

Thanks for the quick summary and the attachments. Initial checks from our side look consistent with what you described — a noticeable spike in 5xx around 22:29 UTC and a handful of user-facing retries.

A couple of questions:
- Did any PII or request payloads get re-sent or duplicated as part of the retry path?
- Will the SDK resilience guidance include recommended backoff/timeout settings for streaming clients?

Please share the longer RCA when available; we'd like to map the mitigations to our incident playbook. If it's easier, I'm happy to do a 30-min readout on Tue 2026-08-24 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Julia Barker
Director of Platform Engineering | CedarBridge
julia.barker@cedarbridge.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Barker <julia.barker@cedarbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident digest: transient session-resync — customer readout & action checklist

Julia — quick answers inline and a short update on deliverables.

> Did any PII or request payloads get re-sent or duplicated as part of the retry path?
Short answer: No user payloads were retransmitted by Redwood services. The retry logic at the edge will re-attempt idempotent inference requests; for streaming sessions, the server signalled a client-side reconnect — the reconnects resumed token streaming but did not replay prior tokens. We're including request-id traces in the PDF.

> Will the SDK resilience guidance include recommended backoff/timeout settings for streaming clients?
Yes — suggested settings + small code snippets will be included in the SDK guidance (target 2026-08-25). We'll also propose a short client-side checksum to detect accidental duplication if you want it.

Update on deliverables:
- Full root-cause report (David) — now uploaded to the Drive link in related_links; PDF attached to this thread.
- Operator playbook & gating (Marissa) — draft complete; will share by 2026-09-01 for your review.
- SDK resilience guidance (Sofia) — draft available 2026-08-25; happy to include a CedarBridge appendix.

We can do Tue 2026-08-24 10:00 PT for the 30-min readout. I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda: 1) timeline walk, 2) forensics summary, 3) proposed mitigations & customer asks.

Thanks for the partnership here — we'll be ready with the evidence and concrete next steps.

Best,
Sofia

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Barker <julia.barker@cedarbridge.com>; Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident digest: transient session-resync — customer readout & action checklist

Julia — adding a couple of operational notes for your runbook team ahead of the readout: 

- Where we saw the failure: Dedicated pool upgrade path (canary batch 3 of 8) — operator should hold upgrades for canary traffic if any worker reports cache miss rates >5% during warmup.
- Short-term guard: we've set a temporary throttle that prevents the reconciliation job from running during active canary upgrades.
- Verification checklist (short):
  * Confirm SDKs reconnect with idempotency keys in place
  * Verify dedicated pool warmup metrics (kv_cache_hit_ratio >= 92%) before allowing new traffic shift
  * Post-upgrade smoke for 15 minutes at 5 QPS before broad rollout

I'll bring the automation PR for the gating rule to our next ops sprint and share a test plan. See you on Tue.

-Marissa
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
